claims.text: Randomly distributed multiple principal elements produce severe lattice distortion in high-entropy alloys.
Severe lattice distortion forces dislocation cores into wavy, non-planar configurations during dynamic loading.
Wavy, non-planar dislocation configurations impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion promotes uniform strain-hardening plasticity.
Uniform strain-hardening plasticity enables high strength and ductility to occur simultaneously.
Homogenized NbTaTiV can form a single-phase BCC high-entropy alloy.
The proposed NbTaTiV specimen is simultaneously in a homogenized and as-cast state.
The NbTaTiV microstructure is chemically disordered.
NbTaTiV can be mechanically tested from room temperature through 900°C while retaining a single BCC phase.
Random fluctuations in atomic sizes and bonding create a complex dislocation-energy landscape in HEAs.
The complex energy landscape causes moving dislocations to curve rather than remain straight.
Curved dislocations have a higher barrier to glide and therefore enhance strength.
Curved dislocations distribute plastic deformation more uniformly and thereby preserve ductility.
Relative to a comparable conventional BCC alloy, the HEA will exhibit higher yield strength.
Relative to a comparable conventional BCC alloy, the HEA will exhibit a higher strain-hardening rate.
In-situ TEM will reveal more wavy, non-planar dislocation structures in the HEA than in the conventional BCC baseline.
The proposed mechanism should remain operative from room temperature to near the alloy's solidus temperature.
Secondary phases or significant precipitation can dominate deformation and invalidate the proposed mechanism.
The quantitative contribution of wavy dislocations and its variation among compositions and processing histories are not established.
Failure to observe either enhanced mechanical properties or distinct wavy dislocations relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The specimen is described as both homogenized and as-cast. Homogenization is a post-casting heat treatment, and the cited specimen was drop-cast and then homogenized for three days rather than tested in its as-cast state.

The specified experimental range ends at about 900°C, whereas the asserted validity boundary extends to near the solidus; no experiment or evidence is supplied for the additional high-temperature range.
